sections.title: DBMS Architecture & Relational Concepts
sections.overview: A Database Management System (DBMS) is software designed to store, retrieve, manage, and query structured data systematically.

coreTerms.desc: A two-dimensional grid composed of rows and columns.
A single row representing one complete data entity record.
A vertical column representing a specific characteristic or property of the entity.
The set of all permissible values that an attribute is allowed to hold.
The total NUMBER OF ATTRIBUTES (columns) in a relation. High-frequency exam question!
The total NUMBER OF TUPLES (rows) in a relation. High-frequency exam question!

keys.name: Super Key
keys.desc: Any set of one or more attributes that can uniquely identify a tuple within a relation.

keys.name: Candidate Key
keys.desc: A minimal Super Key without redundant attributes. A table can have multiple candidate keys.

keys.name: Primary Key
keys.desc: The candidate key specifically chosen by the database designer to uniquely identify records. MUST BE UNIQUE and CANNOT CONTAIN NULL VALUES.

keys.name: Alternate Key
keys.desc: Any candidate key that was NOT chosen as the primary key (Secondary Key).

keys.name: Foreign Key
keys.desc: An attribute in a table that references the Primary Key of another table, establishing a relationship between the two and enforcing Referential Integrity.

keys.name: Composite Key
keys.desc: A primary key composed of two or more attributes together to form a unique identifier.

sections.title: ACID Properties in Transactions
sections.overview: ACID properties ensure reliable processing of database transactions, especially critical in financial and banking software.

properties.name: Atomicity
properties.desc: A transaction must execute completely or not at all. If any step fails (e.g. power loss during money transfer), the entire transaction rolls back to original state.

properties.name: Consistency
properties.desc: A transaction transforms database from one valid consistent state to another, satisfying all integrity constraints (e.g. Total account balances preserved).

properties.name: Isolation
properties.desc: Concurrent execution of multiple transactions results in a system state as if they were executed sequentially. Uncommitted changes are hidden from other transactions.

properties.name: Durability
properties.desc: Once a transaction is committed, its effects are permanently recorded in non-volatile storage and survive any subsequent system crash or power outage.

sections.title: Database Normalization (1NF to BCNF)
sections.purpose: Process of organizing relations to minimize data redundancy (duplicate storage) and eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.

levels.rule: Each column must contain atomic (indivisible) values. No repeating groups or multi-valued attributes allowed.

Must be in 1NF AND have NO Partial Functional Dependencies (no non-prime attribute should depend on a proper subset of candidate key). All non-key attributes must be fully functionally dependent on primary key.
Must be in 2NF AND have NO Transitive Dependencies (no non-prime attribute should determine another non-prime attribute). If X -> Y, then either X is a super key or Y is a prime attribute.
Strict 3.5NF: For every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X MUST be a Super Key.

categories.name: Data Definition Language
categories.desc: Defines and alters database schema and structure.

commands.usage: Creates database objects (tables, views, indexes, schemas).
Modifies structure of existing table (adds, modifies, or drops columns).
Permanently deletes database object and its structure from disk.
Removes all rows from a table rapidly while retaining table structure. Cannot be rolled back in standard DDL.

categories.name: Data Manipulation Language
categories.desc: Manipulates data records stored within relations.

commands.usage: Inserts new rows into a table (`INSERT INTO table VALUES (...)`).
Modifies existing data values in one or more rows (`UPDATE table SET col = val WHERE condition`).
Removes specific rows satisfying a condition (`DELETE FROM table WHERE condition`).
Retrieves records matching criteria (`SELECT cols FROM table WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY`).
Gives user access privileges to database objects.

categories.name: Transaction Control Language
categories.desc: Manages transactional boundaries in DML operations.

commands.usage: Permanently saves all changes of the current transaction to disk.
Undoes all changes made since the last commit or savepoint.
Sets an intermediate checkpoint within a transaction for partial rollback.

dropVsTruncateVsDelete.drop: DDL command. Deletes entire table data AND table schema definition. Cannot be rolled back.
dropVsTruncateVsDelete.truncate: DDL command. Deletes ALL rows at once by deallocating pages; keeps table schema intact. Faster than DELETE.
dropVsTruncateVsDelete.delete: DML command. Deletes specific rows row-by-row based on WHERE clause. Can be rolled back if inside transaction.
